note: Rule lexicon for scripts/vocabulaire.py. Keywords are written readable; matching folds accents, case and punctuation (every non-alphanumeric run is one space) and is word-bounded. A trailing * means word-prefix; # means 1-3 digits. Per type: fr/en = weak keywords (1 point per distinct keyword, at most 2 per title); fr_strong/en_strong = strong keywords (strong_weight points, default 3; institution-context types use 2 so that an action word such as a resignation outranks the institution it happens in; legal-stage types use 4 so a trial outranks the offence it is about). A type is proposed only at 2 points or more; unless = a title containing any of these never scores the type. A title scores a type once (strong beats weak); scores are summed over member titles; ties go to table order (docs/I18N.md table A); zero hits is unclassified. Places: fr/en keyword lists per place code, needs_context = counts only when the same text also names Quebec. All of it is a proposal, never a verdict: an honest unclassified beats a wrong type.
